BPR-max minimizes −log Σⱼ sⱼ sigmoid(rᵢ−rⱼ) + λΣⱼ sⱼrⱼ², with s = softmax over negative scores. Hard negatives receive greater weight, avoiding dilution by many easy negatives. The score penalty pulls negatives toward zero, especially high-scoring ones; it is distinct from weight decay. Official code defaults to bpreg=1.0. Score activation matters: linear, ELU, ReLU and tanh change score ranges, gradients and softmax concentration; official guidance often prefers ELU-0.5 or ELU-1. The negative-weight softmax is separate from this output activation. [Paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [official guidance](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec)

Established sampling combines other minibatch targets—approximately popularity-distributed negatives—with additional samples shared across the minibatch, drawn proportional to item support^α. Additional sampling increases hard-negative coverage without increasing batch size; α=0 is uniform, α=1 popularity-based. Official defaults include 2,048 additional samples and α=0.75. The original Theano implementation samples with replacement, retains duplicates, and masks only the designated target diagonal: duplicate copies of the target can remain among negatives. Repeated items consequently receive extra aggregate softmax weight; these are not unique candidate sets. [Official implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/master/gru4rec.py)

Thus, 128 uniform, target-excluding draws per transition with λ=0 change sample count, distribution, sharing and collision handling, and remove explicit score control. Replacement itself is established practice. Inference from the objective: removing the penalty leaves common score shifts unconstrained, while score scaling still changes sigmoid margins and hard-negative concentration. Uniform sampling can supply fewer informative negatives, slowing learning; instability or inferior validation accuracy is possible, not guaranteed. [Paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf)
